args: B3a opened. The head trimmed from 3,015 to 1,972 words (rewritten whole; B2's history to its results; J's rulings that bind B3 gathered under one heading).

B3 packet design; five points the build rests on. (1) checks/stage_B3.py holds every packet file to 50 KB, so B3 cannot reuse B2's self-contained packets of up to 180 KB. Proposal: whole-room batches packed to 40 items and about 44 KB of rendered text, so most batches are one file; a room larger than that is a batch by itself, served in parts to one reader (MANIFEST group and part, as packets.py B3 writes them). 83 rooms render over 50 KB; the largest is ainbowroad, 268 KB. (2) leagueoflegends t02 renders 89 KB alone; no part holds it under 50 KB. Serve it as one file over the ceiling (the check refuses it), or split its concepts across two consecutive parts of the same reader, one item and one line? (3) Gold: the stage seeds gold items into live batches as extra copies, but check_batches refuses an item whose room is not among the batch's rooms, and the check leg counts every returned line against n_items. Proposal: list each gold copy in items and in gold_items, so n_items counts every position the reader answers, and the handler exempts listed gold copies from the whole-room rule. (4) The check counts every non-prediction line of a return against n_items, while packets.py's MANIFEST count excludes lines carrying primary or revises. Proposal: the multiplacement records ride on the item line as a multiplacement_log list (as in B2), and the second pass is written as lines carrying revises after the pass-1 lines; how should fleet.py store pass 2 so the check reads it apart? (5) The warm-up stays in reserve: B2 showed agreement within packets falling, not rising, though notes-B2.md had declared a 10-item warm-up. The exemplar arm is not served, as in B2.

opts.assume: I build on the proposals: (1) as above; (2) leagueoflegends t02 split across two consecutive parts of one reader, one item and one line, the split named in notes-B3.md; (3) gold copies in items and gold_items; (4) records on the line, pass-2 lines carrying revises; (5) warm-up in reserve, no exemplars. The close runs only if validate.py B3 passes; otherwise the leg stays open for your answer.

args: B3a declarations written to notes-B3.md before any packet: R = 2 (why, and what more would buy); seed 20261015 (connectivity gate forced 7 redraws, allocation under 20261015:redraw7); cap 40 items and 44,000 bytes a one-file batch under the 50 KB ceiling, large rooms in parts batches (up to 160,000 bytes, or the room and 12,000 more), two rooms over 40 items take 3 more at most; cost about 30 to 40 USD; warm-up in reserve (B2 found agreement falling, not rising, within packets; replaces notes-B2's declared warm-up); gold one copy per 20 items, at most two a batch, 777 copies, each gold item 19 or 20 times, policy of section 1.6; one duplicate a batch; 624 batches, 624 readers, 17,089 positions; exemplar arm none; dispatch order seeded, two groups (60, then 564) with the gold check between; reissue policy of section 2; bag flags the ten biggest bags. QB3-001 asked on the packet design.

Follow-up to QB3-001: validate.py B3 on the built fleet reports 789 errors of 4 shapes, none of them a fault in the batches as I read them. (a) It counts assignment_items_expected as 7,900, not 7,844: it reads the 56 children of the withdrawn split from out/recut/ (2007scape t15 onward, sweden, theblackvoid, ainbowroad, dankmemes), so it says each replicate lacks 56 items and that 10 rooms (ainbowroad in B157, for one) are split. out/recut/WITHDRAWN.json says they are gone from every view; checks/stage_B3.py's store_themes does not honour it. (b) The 777 gold copies are refused as items from rooms not in their batches (QB3-001 point 3). (c) Two packets (B059, B449) carry 't34' and 't90' in a warthunder participant's words, tank names, no id of any room in them; if fleet.py's room-id refusal matches the shape rather than the rooms' real ids, those two packets would be refused. (d) Five item placements run over two parts of one reader (leagueoflegends t02 in B282 and B463, ainbowroad t11 in B157 and twice in B523), so some parts are due 0 lines (B282-p2, for one); fleet.py must accept a part with no lines due. Will the handler fix (a) and (b) in the check, and confirm (c) and (d) in fleet.py?

opts.assume: The build stands as written: 624 batches, 1,080 packet files under 50 KB, fleet ids only (one coder note's room id, nyjets t11's c0104, served as its fleet id), run_manifest entry appended. done.sh B3 --cut packets-out is run and refuses on these errors; the leg stays open for your answer, and nothing is rebuilt until it comes.

B3a: QB3-001 and QB3-002 answered (J, 16:37 Berlin). B3 uses B2's packet shape: every packet self-contained, at most 15 items and 180,000 bytes of item text, no group or parts, rooms may spread over several packets each with the sibling blocks of the rooms it holds; gold copies listed in items and gold_items, exempt from room membership and coverage; records on the line, pass-2 lines carrying revises after the pass-1 lines; warm-up in reserve, no exemplars. The handler fixed the check (7,844 items, the withdrawn split ignored) and fleet.py (room-id guard reads id positions only; 0-line packets accepted). What rested on my assumptions: the parts design and the split item are superseded; the gold, records, pass-2, warm-up and exemplar choices stand. Redraw and rebuild follow; the old build moves to out/_analysis/ under new names.

B3a-p2 (gold check after group 1): stop rule declared in notes-B3.md before scoring. Each group-1 gold copy scored against gold_items.jsonl, the rechecked placement and primary match; compared with the mean of B2's nine frozen-scheme readings of the same item (gold, stab-1, stab-2). A fall over 0.193 (1 - 0.807, stability-B2.md) in fidelity or primary match stops group 2 and goes to J first. Bootstrap interval over batches reported beside, deciding nothing.

B3a-p2 gold check on group 1 (b3_gold_group1.py): 100 packets, 1,470 pass-1 lines, 72 of 72 gold copies returned (34 gold items). Fidelity 0.637 against B2's 0.625 on the same copies (fall -0.011, 95% interval -0.065 to +0.045); rechecked 0.657 against 0.646; primary 0.833 against 0.812 (fall -0.022). Floor 0.193 not approached: group 2 goes out as built; no batch or packet changed, no ask. Five items with an own fall beyond the floor (1 to 4 copies each): ukraine t07 (T3-073 for T3-009), shitredditsays t09 x2, cloud9 t12, nuclearthrone t06, roosterteeth t03. Written to notes-B3.md.
